title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: 2020 economic contraction figures
sections.summary: The economy contracted 12.6% in the second quarter of 2020 and 5.4% overall for 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The economy went into a nose dive with the steepest contraction recorded in the second quarter of 2020 at -12.6% and an overall contraction of -5.4% for the whole of 2020.

sections.label: EDB 2020 investment commitments
sections.summary: EDB attracted $17.2 billion in investment commitments in 2020, creating 19,000 jobs when implemented, and foreign tech giants set up in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In 2020, despite being the year of the global pandemic, EDB was able to attract investment commitments of $17.2 billion, which, when these projects are fully implemented, will create 19,000 new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: A case in point is Singapore's continued ability to attract foreign tech giants to set up here in 2020—such as the likes of ByteDance, Amazon, Twitter, Zoom, Tencent, among others.

sections.label: Risk-sharing arrangements with capital providers
sections.summary: Risk-sharing arrangements include the Venture Debt Programme, Emerging Technology Programme, and a Local Enterprises Funding Platform with $500 million each from Government and Temasek.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Some of the risk-sharing arrangements with market providers of capital includes the Venture Debt Programme for high-growth enterprises, co-funding the transformation of mature enterprises under the Emerging Technology Programme or the Local Enterprises Funding Platform where the Government and Temasek Holdings will co-invest $500 million each.

sections.label: Seizing global supply chain opportunities
sections.summary: It asks how Singapore companies can seize global supply chain opportunities and calls for bold steps, new capabilities, and positioning for growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: How can Singapore companies seize these opportunities in the reordering and reorganisation of the global supply chain and be plugged into the critical parts of the global networks?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We need to take bold steps to seize new opportunities, invest in new capabilities and be well positioned for the next bound of growth.

sections.label: Singapore certification framework proposal
sections.summary: It asks whether Singapore can work towards a certification framework for companies, especially SMEs, similar to Swiss Label and Brand K.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can we work towards a Singapore certification framework that provides Singapore companies, especially our SMEs, a quality certification for their products and services, similar to the Swiss Label and the Brand K initiatives in Switzerland and Korea respectively?

sections.label: Timing loan scheme withdrawal
sections.summary: An SBF survey found 38% of transactions paid on time and almost 50% of late payments over 30 days past due, so loan scheme withdrawal must be timed carefully.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: According to an SBF National Business Survey, only 38% of total transactions were paid on time, and almost 50% of late payments were above 30 days past due, on top of the credit terms already offered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is critical to time the withdrawal of loan schemes carefully, including the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme (TBLP) and SME Working Capital Loan, in order to ensure the much-needed relief in cash flows does not vanish suddenly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government has sent a strong signal that it will back firms, support firms, that are ready to transform in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I especially welcome the Local Enterprises Funding Platform to support large local enterprises from the more traditional sectors with $1 billion in Government and Temasek funding.

sections.label: SME relief and capex grants
sections.summary: With JSS winding down, the speaker suggests enhancing the enterprise development grant to help SMEs with capex investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) was a key support for these companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But with JSS winding down except for the hard-hit sectors, SMEs will need added relief support through grants and loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As they are preoccupied with surviving the crisis, investment in capex is likely to take a backseat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I suggest that we can enhance our enterprise development grant to help SMEs with their capex investment.

sections.label: Facebook small businesses programme
sections.summary: Facebook announced a small businesses programme supporting companies with cash and ad credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Late last year, Facebook announced a small businesses programme that supported companies with cash and ad credits.

sections.label: Dynamic comparative advantage for Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore should create dynamic comparative advantage as a small open innovation-driven economy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The answer, to answer this question, I believe, is that we should create dynamic comparative advantage as a small open innovation-driven economy.

sections.label: Human capital and digital infrastructure
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore's human capital base and digital infrastructure investment can help entrepreneurs reach overseas markets.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, our large human capital base and investment in digital infrastructure can enable our entrepreneurs to reach overseas markets.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreements and clean tech R&D
sections.summary: The speaker cites Digital Economy Agreements with Australia, New Zealand and Chile, and urban design investment facilitating clean technology R&D.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, let me acknowledge the advantages that Digital Economy Agreements, already established with Australia, New Zealand and Chile, confer to our local firms an advantage in their internationalisation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, our investment in urban design to make Singapore environmentally-friendly with a low carbon footprint can facilitate research and development (R&D) in clean technology.

sections.label: SMEs' share of economy
sections.summary: SMEs made up 72% of employment and 44% of added nominal value in 2019 and also received support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SMEs, which are the backbone of our economy, making up 72% of employment and 44% of added nominal value in 2019, also received support.

sections.label: Incentives for MNC-SME collaboration
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an additional, selective incentive tier for MNCs that partner with local SMEs, citing PACT and past LIUP schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As I argued in my Budget speech, can incentive packages for MNCs include an additional tier of incentive if the MNCs work with local SMEs in executing the investment project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This additional tier can be offered very selectively where there are good local SMEs that can be partners to MNCs and it should be meant as a nudge and encouragement, not mandate or dicta.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are schemes like PACT which reward MNC and SME collaboration, just like there were schemes like LIUP in the past.

sections.label: Auditing schemes and manufacturing sector
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether economic agencies audit these schemes' costs against benefits, noting manufacturing is 21% of GDP and employs over 450,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last but not least, do our economic agencies regularly audit these schemes to weigh the cost in terms of cash outlay and so on, versus the benefit in terms of job creation and economic multipliers?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the manufacturing sector contributes 21% of Singapore’s GDP and employs over 450,000 people.

sections.label: Smart Industry Readiness Index transformation
sections.summary: Singapore's Smart Industry Readiness Index catalysed manufacturing companies' transformation around Industry 4.0's process, technology and organisation pillars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Singapore’s Smart Industry Readiness Index (SIRI) catalysed the transformation of companies in the manufacturing sector around the three pillars of Industry 4.0 – around process, technology and organisation.

sections.label: Budget 2021 enterprise funding measures
sections.summary: Budget 2021 introduced the Local Enterprises Funding Platform and enhanced the Venture Debt Programme to help SMEs access capital to expand overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Budget 2021 has introduced the new Local Enterprises Funding Platform to support large local enterprises and enhanced the Venture Debt Programme to help SMEs access necessary capital to expand overseas and to seize opportunities.

sections.label: SME digitalisation transformation progress
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for an update on SMEs' adoption of digital solutions to improve productivity amid manpower and cashflow challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, with digitalisation and the structural changes in industries, can Minister provide an update on the progress of businesses transformation of companies especially SMEs in the adoption of digital solutions to improve productivity in the face of manpower and cashflow challenges?

sections.label: RIE spending and foreign researchers
sections.summary: Between 2005 and 2020, $55 billion was spent on RIE, and Budget calls for $2.2 billion on talent development, with many foreigners among researchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Between 2005 and 2020, we have spent a total of $55 billion on RIE, an amount larger than the drawdown of reserves to fight the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The budget also calls for $2.2 billion to be spent on "talent development", including postgraduate scholarships, but the majority of the postgraduate students, researchers and faculty members are foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the NUS' Centre for Quantum Technologies established in 2007, 74% of its researchers and postgraduate students are foreigners in 2019, a decade after its establishment.

sections.label: Tax credit for ventures
sections.summary: Proposes tax credit to activate access capital for ventures and higher taxes on passive capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A better alternative is to provide tax credit to activate access capital in our system to fund the ventures and increase taxes on passive capital that do not.

sections.label: Singapore R&D spending comparison
sections.summary: In 2017 Singapore's research expenditure was just under 2% of national output, below the 2.3% global average and other economies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2017, our national expenditure on research and expenditure, as a share of national output, amounted to a low shy of 2%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This amount is actually below the global average of 2.3% and, perhaps, more tellingly, for a nation that seeks to be a knowledge-based economy is also significantly below the amounts that other technology-seeking economies have devoted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The United States, for example, spends 2.8%, Japan 3.2%, Korea 4.6% and Israel 4.8%.

sections.label: MTI R&D and investment figures
sections.summary: Asks what conditions would make MTI target higher R&D spending, citing 2020 investment and job figures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under what conditions will MTI be willing to target and increase an R&D expenditure to bring us closer to the spending for technology driven economies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, in a Straits Times article on 21 Jan 2021, MTI declared that Singapore managed to attract about $17.2 billion in fixed asset investments in 2020, despite weathering its worst recession since Independence as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such achievements must have come through great efforts by the working staff of luring and convincing investors to invest in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We were also made known that such investments, when completed, would lead to the creation of more than 19,000 new high quality jobs over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We note that close to a quarter of the new jobs would be digital roles, such as cloud developers, software engineers and cybersecurity specialists.

sections.label: Bridging worker skillset gaps
sections.summary: Asks how the Labour Movement and training associations can collaborate with agencies like EDB to bridge skillset gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On this point, I would like to ask how the Labour Movement and our training associations like NTUC Learning Hub can collaborate with Government agencies like EDB and other key partners, to bridge the skillset gaps to ensure that we prepare our workers to seize the job opportunities and allow Singaporeans to form the core of the company workforce.

sections.label: Renewed social compact
sections.summary: Calls for stakeholders to work on a renewed social compact, noting TACs signed a joint statement on fair hiring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: I believe that now is the time for stakeholders to work on a renewed social compact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: And as I said in my Budget debate speech, I have highlighted two points: 29 TACs including SBF have signed a joint statement in support of fair hiring and employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Businesses must play their part to have fair practice in the workplace, and develop local talent and leadership.

sections.label: Budget 2021 elements and Fund
sections.summary: Says Budget 2021 has elements of Tech, Skills, Capital and Vision, and the Fund will invest in LLEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Budget 2021 has the critical elements of Tech + Skills + Capital + Vision for Singapore to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: This Fund will invest in LLEs and support their growth.

sections.label: SMEs hire workforce share
sections.summary: SMEs hire more than 70% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: SMEs do hire more than 70% of our workforce.

sections.label: Director of local SME
sections.summary: The speaker declares being a director of a local SME providing technology consulting services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I declare that I am a director of a local SME providing technology consulting services.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore assisting SME managers
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore could assist more SME managers to adopt modern management practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, Enterprise Singapore could assist more SME managers to adopt modern management practices.

sections.label: AI competence centers and coaches
sections.summary: An example is the first 26 AI competence centers with 20 AI coaches training 1,000 SMEs yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: An example would be the first 26 AI competence centers, staffed with 20 AI coaches to train 1,000 SMEs each year.

sections.label: Supporting enterprises innovation and PACT
sections.summary: The speaker seeks updates on government support for enterprise innovation, global growth, and PACT grant take-up rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to seek the Minister for Trade and Industry's update on how the Government is supporting enterprises to commercialise and capture value from innovative ideas generated from R&D; how we can help our enterprises grow innovation capabilities; how local enterprises can be supported to grow and build capabilities to compete globally; and finally, how to support and transform and seize opportunities to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, as no one single economic entity can be self sufficient and survive in a silo – just as humans require some form of interaction with one another – every business needs to collaborate and coexist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hence would like to ask the Ministry on the existing take-up rate of Partnership for Capability Transformation (PACT) grants and how many of the applicants involve companies collaborating across industry verticals.

sections.label: Tourism sector and SME support
sections.summary: The speaker asks about tourism sector plans, financing for tourism SMEs and hotels, and regional partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With that in mind, what are the short to long-term plans for the tourism sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How can we help the financing structures for tourism SMEs and hotels and to integrate new digital capabilities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Are there plans to partner with other regional tourism boards in other companies and corporates to give the sector a much-needed boost in the post-COVID-19 environment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: One SME restaurant chain owner mentioned to me about how JSS helped her business stay afloat and survive the most difficult period last year, allowing the SME to retain over 50 staff to reach the stage now where the business is seeing some improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: The key measures of help from the Resilience Package such as the JSS and Government loan schemes such as the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme, will end by 30 September 2021.

sections.label: Tourism industry low demand
sections.summary: Border controls and travel restrictions will take longer to normalise, so tourism will bear low demand longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: As border controls and travel restrictions will take a lot longer to normalise, given the pandemic situation outside of Singapore, this means that the tourism industry will have to bear longer the low demand for their services.

sections.label: SME restaurant e-ordering use
sections.summary: Restaurant SMEs increasingly use e-menus, but e-ordering solutions and analytics use is much lower despite productivity benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Taking an example from SMEs in the restaurant business, we are seeing an increased use of e-menus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: However, the use of e-ordering solutions and analytics is way lower even though it helps productivity and can even help supplement the lack of manpower and wait staff.

sections.label: Singapore business hub strategies
sections.summary: Singapore aims to be a global business and technology hub, entrench in value chains, and build capabilities, attracting $17.2 billion investments in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, strengthen our position as a global hub for business and technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second, entrench ourselves as a critical node in global value chains to make us hard to displace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Third, build real and unique capabilities in our enterprises and workers so they can compete in a more globalised world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har asked how Singapore has performed as a business hub amidst COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have attracted in 2020, $17.2 billion worth of Fixed Asset Investments and $6.8 billion in Total Business Expenditure.

sections.label: New competitiveness factors
sections.summary: Beyond quality and cost, speed to evolve products, penetrate markets, supply chain resilience and ideas matter as intellectual capital overtakes physical capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: While quality and cost competitiveness will continue to remain as important factors, other more important factors have arisen: the speed to evolve new products, the speed to penetrate new markets, the resilience of supply chains and the quality of new ideas, as intellectual capital will increasingly overtake physical and financial capital as the defining competitive yardstick.

sections.label: Entrenching in global value chains
sections.summary: Singapore pursues critical capabilities in chosen industries and entrenches in global value chain niches, needing intellectual property for chips and machines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But, instead of just pursuing new "sunrise" industries, we also need to pursue critical capabilities needed to anchor ourselves in every industry that we choose to compete in – be they "sunrise" or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: That is why our second strategy is to entrench ourselves in the critical niches of the global value chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Over the long term, what is important is whether we have access to the intellectual property to produce the chips and the intellectual property to build those machines that produce the chips.

sections.label: Risks to reputation and ecosystem
sections.summary: Wrong things like inconsistent policies and wrong signals can damage Singapore's reputation and ecosystem, causing quick loss.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If we do the wrong things and damage this reputation and ecosystem, we can quickly lose it all. "Wrong things" include inconsistent policies on business, taxation, manpower and talent. "Wrong things" include sending the world the wrong signals that detract from our intent to enable our companies to form globally competitive talent teams to compete with the world.

sections.label: Funding to MNCs and SMEs
sections.summary: In the last five years, around $13 billion went to MNCs and $21 billion to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In the last five years, we gave around $13 billion to MNCs and $21 billion to SMEs.

sections.label: MNCs working with local companies
sections.summary: MNCs that do well are more likely to work with local companies, and the PACT programme supports knowledge transfer to SMEs and start-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: When MNCs here do well, they are more likely to work with local companies, source from them and have them as part of the value-chain and supply chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We also encourage MNCs to work with SMEs through the PACT programme, which supports knowledge transfer between larger companies and local SMEs or start-ups.

sections.label: Medium-sized enterprise scale-up programmes
sections.summary: The goal is more medium-sized enterprises bulked up to compete in niche areas beyond Singapore, via Scale-up SG, Enterprise Leadership Transformation, GlobalConnect@SBF and the Southeast Asia Manufacturing Alliance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For medium-sized enterprises, our goal is to have more of them and bulk them up to compete in niche areas, beyond Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This why we embarked on the Scale-up SG and Enterprise Leadership Transformation programmes to build deep capabilities for them to compete on a global scale.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We also aim to help them internationalise by bringing them together to compete overseas with programmes such as GlobalConnect@SBF, and the Southeast Asia Manufacturing Alliance.

sections.label: Company transformation projects with ESG support
sections.summary: Over 15,000 companies embarked on transformation projects with ESG's support in 2020, 50% higher than 2019, and Scale-up SG aims to groom another 50 local champions in two years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Over 15,000 companies embarked on transformation projects with ESG’s support in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In spite of the crisis, this is 50% higher than even in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In particular, through Scale-up SG, we aim to groom another 50 future local champions over the next two years.

sections.label: AfA 11-11 campaign
sections.summary: The AfA launched an online-offline 11 November campaign, 11-11, with gamification elements for retailers and consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The AfA had launched an online-offline 11 November campaign, 11-11, incorporating gamification elements to provide retailers with more marketing opportunities and deliver consumers a whole new experience.

sections.label: Financing ecosystem and EFS-VDP
sections.summary: The Government monitors the financing ecosystem so all companies can access capital, and extended the EFS-VDP, raising the maximum supportable loan quantum from $5 million to $8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government carefully monitors our financing ecosystem to ensure that all companies – from start-ups to SMEs to LLEs – can access the capital that they need.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have extended the Enterprise Financing Scheme-Venture Debt Programme (EFS-VDP) and raise the maximum supportable loan quantum from $5 million to $8 million.

sections.label: LEFP investing in local enterprises
sections.summary: The LEFP will use Temasek's network and expertise to seek out promising LLEs to invest in, focusing on growth-aligned sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is where the LEFP comes in to precisely address and meet this need.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, drawing on the network and expertise of Temasek, the LEFP will actively seek out promising LLEs to invest in, focusing on sectors that are aligned with the engines of growth in our economy.

sections.label: Government R&D spending commitment
sections.summary: The Government commits to investing about 1% of GDP in research, innovation and enterprise over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government is committed to investing about 1% of our GDP in research, innovation and enterprise over the next five years.

sections.label: Business R&D expenditure growth
sections.summary: Business expenditure on R&D rose more than two-and-a-half times, from $1.5 billion in 1998 to about $5.6 billion in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, business expenditure on R&D has increased by more than two-and-a-half times, from $1.5 billion in 1998 to approximately $5.6 billion in 2018.

sections.label: Research scientists and engineers numbers
sections.summary: The number of Research Scientists and Engineers nearly tripled from about 12,700 to over 36,000 between 1998 and 2018, with 70% citizens or PRs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In fact, the number of Research Scientists and Engineers (RSEs) has almost tripled from about 12,700 to over 36,000 in the last 20 years, from 1998 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And 70% of this group of 36,000 are either Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

sections.label: Fortitude COVID-19 test kits
sections.summary: Biomedical R&D capabilities built over 20 years enabled development and manufacture of Fortitude COVID-19 tests, selling over five million units in 45 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, when the world was short of COVID-19 test kits, our biomedical science R&D capabilities built up over the past 20 years have enabled us to develop and manufacture Fortitude COVID-19 diagnostic tests, which have since sold more than five million units in over 45 countries.

sections.label: Expanding Global Innovation Alliance network
sections.summary: The Global Innovation Alliance network will expand from 15 to 25 cities over five years to support enterprises' global outreach and innovation partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will do more to support our companies to internationalise and seize opportunities globally.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will expand the Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) network from 15 to 25 cities over the next five years to support enterprises’ ambitions to expand their global market outreach and seek innovation partnerships.

sections.label: Global Ready Talent programme
sections.summary: Since its 2019 launch, GRT has helped over a thousand Singapore enterprises create opportunities for close to 6,000 students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Through the Global Ready Talent (GRT) programme, our students and young professionals can gain greater exposure and deeper in-market knowledge, and thereafter, become strong contributors to their employers’ global expansion efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And since the launch in 2019, GRT has supported more than a thousand Singapore enterprises in creating such opportunities for close to 6,000 students.

sections.label: GlobalConnect@SBF advisory initiative
sections.summary: SBF partnered ESG to launch GlobalConnect@SBF, whose market advisors supported more than 2,500 Singapore businesses despite challenging 2020 conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: One example is how the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) has partnered ESG to launch its GlobalConnect@SBF initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This initiative, through their team of market advisors, providing targeted advisory services, has since supported more than 2,500 Singapore businesses in spite of the challenging conditions in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Supported by all these efforts, our common vision of success is to have an eco-system of resilient enterprises that are highly capable, that are open to collaboration, and that are equipped to compete globally.

sections.label: Agri-food tech co-investment partners
sections.summary: ESG and SEEDS Capital appointed seven co-investment partners to encourage early-stage equity investments into Singapore-based agri-food tech start-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: To encourage early-stage equity investments into Singapore-based agri-food tech start-ups, ESG collaborated with SEEDS Capital to appoint seven co-investment partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We expect this to translate into more than $90 million of investments.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme for tourism
sections.summary: In 2020 over 7,000 tourism businesses were supported to retain locals, and JSS will be extended six months with 30% and 10% wage support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In 2020, we supported over 7,000 tourism businesses to retain locals through our Jobs Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will extend the JSS by six months to support our tourism sector, as Deputy Prime Minister Heng has suggested.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Tourism firms will receive 30% support for wages paid from April to June 2021, and 10% support for wages paid from July to September 2021.

sections.label: Tourism Recovery Action Task Force
sections.summary: Last February a task force of Government and industry tourism leaders was set up to identify opportunities and co-create solutions for border reopening.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Last February, we set up the Tourism Recovery Action Task Force, comprising tourism leaders from Government and industry, to identify opportunities and to co-create solutions to ensure that our tourism sector is well-placed when borders reopen.

sections.label: Local tech talent pipeline
sections.summary: Over three years, IHLs will generate around 20,000 local tech talent, supplemented by at least 6,250 from WSG and IMDA place-and-train programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Over the next three years, our IHLs will generate around 20,000 local tech talent, supplemented by at least 6,250 from WSG’s and IMDA’s place-and-train programmes in functions such as Software Engineering and Cybersecurity.

sections.label: Tech.Pass for global talent
sections.summary: Tech.Pass lets top-tier global talent contribute as founder, employee, consultant or academic, and interest has been keen since applications opened in mid-July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: As I did; and as some Members in this House, including Ms Janet Ang in IBM and Ms Jessica Tan in Microsoft did.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: So, one way to ensure top talent joins Team Singapore is through Tech.Pass and Tech.Pass which allows high-achieving, top-tier global talent to contribute to our economy in multiple ways as a founder, employee, consultant and academic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: To Ms Foo Mee Har's question, we have seen keen interest in Tech.Pass since applications opened in mid-July and we will continue to evaluate the scheme.

sections.label: Attach-and-Train for robotic engineers
sections.summary: Sectors like Advanced Manufacturing demand automation and design engineers, and the Attach-and-Train programme lets Singaporeans learn robotics through on-the-job attachments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Sectors, such as Advanced Manufacturing, continue to see strong demand for automation engineers and design engineers and skillsets such as programming and 3D modelling and we have initiatives to help jobseekers gain these required skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For example, under the Attach-and-Train programme for robotic engineers, Singaporeans can learn robotics and automation technologies through on the job training attachments at host companies.

sections.label: Government support for transformation
sections.summary: The Government will stand with businesses and people to keep Singapore a global centre for business, innovation and talent, while local businesses must also transform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In this transformation, our Government will stand shoulder to shoulder with our businesses and our people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will and must ensure that Singapore continues to be a global centre for business, innovation and talent, where local and global talent can live, work and play.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In my maiden Parliament speech, I likened Singapore to the Starship Enterprise – diverse in talent, always exploring new frontiers, boldly going where no one has gone before and breaking through the crisis before us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: But we cannot be a global node without also transforming our local businesses.

sections.label: SMEs role in economic recovery
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of enterprises and contribute 72% of employment, and will play a pivotal role in economic recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: SMEs will continue to play a pivotal role in the recovery of our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: They make up 99% of our enterprises, of our companies and contribute 72% of employment.

sections.label: Engagement of heartland shops
sections.summary: As of February 2021, more than 85% of heartland shops have been engaged, with the target on track to be met this month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As of February 2021, we have engaged more than 85% of these heartland shops and are on track to meet our target this month.

sections.label: E-payments and sales growth
sections.summary: Up to 25% of sales now use e-payments, and revenue rose 10% in the first three months of going digital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Today, up to 25% of their sales use e-payments and revenue has gone up by 10% in the first three months of going digital.

sections.label: PSG enhanced support extended
sections.summary: PSG's enhanced maximum support level of up to 80% is extended till 31 March 2022 to help more enterprises transform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To help more enterprises transform, we are extending PSG's enhanced maximum support level of up to 80% till 31 March 2022.

sections.label: Over 230,000 unique visits
sections.summary: Since its launch last August, it has received over 230,000 unique visits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since its launch last August, it has received over 230,000 unique visits.

sections.label: TAC competency framework development
sections.summary: A TAC competency framework led by SCCCI with support from SBF, BSG and SSG will be developed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Recognising this need, a TAC competency framework, led by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI), with the support from the Singapore Business Federation (SBF), BSG and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), will be developed.

sections.label: TAC skillsets upgrade programmes
sections.summary: Suitable programmes will be developed to upgrade TAC sector skillsets, with the framework expected ready in the third quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Suitable programmes will then be developed to upgrade and build the skillsets of the TAC sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This competency framework is expected to be ready in the third quarter of this year and we strongly encourage our TACs to adopt it to upskill their staff.

sections.label: SME Centres specialised advisory pilot
sections.summary: SME Centres would begin piloting specialised advisory services to support enterprises in areas such as digitalisation and financing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: First, SME Centres would begin piloting specialised advisory services to support enterprises in specific areas such as digitalisation and financing.

sections.label: No return to pre-COVID world
sections.summary: There will be no return to a pre-COVID-19 world and enterprises must transform, with MTI, ESG and economic agencies working with enterprises, TACs and industries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Chairman, in closing, there will be no return to a pre-COVID-19 world and our enterprises must seize the initiative to transform their business models to secure the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Rest assured that MTI, ESG and the various economic agencies will work hand in hand with our enterprises, TACs and industries to co-create, innovate and unlock new opportunities for growth.

sections.label: CPTPP membership interest
sections.summary: Singapore welcomes countries meeting CPTPP standards to join, but says it is premature to conclude on US interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Recently, I think Members would have heard the interest of the United Kingdom and even China to join the CPTPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: From Singapore's perspective, we welcome all countries who are able to meet the high standards of CPTPP to join us so that we can continue to enlarge the partnership for the benefit of all members and also to have more certainty for a rule-based trading order in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With respect to the US' interest or renewed interest to return to the TPP or CPTPP, at this point in time, I think it would be premature for us to come to any conclusion.

sections.label: Return to pre-COVID GDP
sections.summary: With good progress by late this year or early next year, GDP should quantitatively return to pre-COVID-19 level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, on the second question that Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked, indeed, quantitatively, with good progress towards the end of this year or the early part of next year, we should be able to get back to the same GDP level as the pre-COVID-19 level, quantitatively.

sections.label: Benchmarking output and outcomes
sections.summary: The answer is yes; achievements are benchmarked from input, output and outcome perspectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The answer to Mr Leon Perera's question is definitely yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We definitely benchmark what we achieve, not just from the input perspective, but from the output and also, most importantly, from the outcome perspective.

sections.label: Reviewing schemes and resources
sections.summary: MTI constantly reviews schemes to apply finite resources best to grow enterprises as an eco-system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It may not be causal, but it will, at least, give us a sense of whether we are making progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And that is why, during my speech, I mentioned that, at every point in time, MTI is constantly reviewing our schemes to make sure that we apply the finite resources to the best use in order to grow our enterprise as an eco-system.

sections.label: Review in process
sections.summary: A review is currently in the process.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In fact, we are in the process of reviewing.

sections.label: Update in coming months
sections.summary: Overlapping areas may offer new opportunities, and the House should be updated a few months into the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And to the extent that is possible, we could even have overlapping areas in which we can find new opportunities to branch into.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, I think, in time to come, we should be able to update the House a few months into the future.

sections.label: Niche R&D competitive advantage
sections.summary: Singapore focuses R&D on niche areas like RF modules where it has competitive advantage based on intellectual property, not size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But there are certain niche areas that we have the capability and where we focus our R&D into those capabilities, for example, the RF modules, so that we can carve out a niche for ourselves in those very specific areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we look for areas whereby we have a competitive advantage, not based on size, but based on our intellectual property.

sections.label: Expensive machine part cost
sections.summary: A part that looks innocuous is the most expensive, costing more than 10% of the entire machine's price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It looks rather innocuous, but it is the most expensive part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It costs about more than 10% of the price of the entire machine.

sections.label: Country captures niche part
sections.summary: A country making that part captured a niche area few can do, so machines worldwide ultimately return to that supplier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But that particular country that made that particular part of the machine has captured a very niche area that very few can do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That even if machines come from different parts of the world, they, ultimately, go back to that same supplier.

sections.label: Downstream funding private sector
sections.summary: Going downstream toward innovation and commercialisation, funding initiatives would include a private sector participation component.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But as we go downstream towards the innovation and commercialisation possibilities, we would have to crowd in more of this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why, as a strategy, as we go downstream, our funding of many of these initiatives, we would like to have a funding component that sees the private sector participation.

sections.label: Tech.Pass applications approved
sections.summary: Since launching in mid-January this year, about 22 Tech.Pass applications have been approved thus far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since we launched it in mid-January this year, we have approved about 22 applications for the Tech.Pass, thus far.

sections.label: Monitoring Tech.Pass adjustments
sections.summary: The fast, dynamic tech sector requires monitoring Tech.Pass, with 22 currently, and adjusting which tech professionals to attract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But the tech sector is very fast and is very dynamic and so, we will have to monitor how the Tech.Pass is working.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Thus far, we currently have 22, but we will have to adjust and see what kind of tech professionals we want to attract in, assess the viability and also assess how they are doing within the parameters that we have set up.

sections.label: Expanding cities globally
sections.summary: The speaker says they are expanding from 15 cities globally to 25.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As I have alluded to earlier on, we are expanding them from 15 cities globally to 25.

sections.label: Know-who and market access
sections.summary: SBF works closely with ESG to help deep-tech companies gain market access and navigate different countries' regulations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The most important part at the end – so, you have the knowledge, you have the know-how – I think given the fact that we are a very small market, we need to tap globally, we go on to the next step and into the know-who.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, I think it is not just important for you to have knowledge and know-how, someone many years ago, an entrepreneur told me that, "You need to not just have knowledge, you need to know how, but you also need know-who." For that part, we have the SBF working very closely with the ESG to establish whether it is from the point of view of service centres to guide many of these deep-tech companies – how to gain market access into many of these markets, but at the same time, also to sort of help them to navigate the difficulties of working through the different regulation, the legislature of different countries and so on, to penetrate these markets and gain acceptance.

sections.label: Intensified global digital competition
sections.summary: Competition is more global, digital, and about resilience and safety, so they must move nimbly, fast and together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Competition has intensified, it will be more global not local.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It will be much more digital not physical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It will not just be about cost and efficiency, but also about resilience and safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To win, we must move nimbly, move fast, move together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We must distinguish ourselves as a safe harbour for capital talent and intellectual property.
